requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
rationale:
I found no gap. Every obligation in `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` maps to code reachable from its {impl} items, and each has a test carrying a {test} reference.

**Implementation**
- **Scope of parsing.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[inspect_repository_with_progress]` passes the discovered files to `crate::rust_coverage::validate_rust_functions`, and carries an {impl} reference to this requirement. `rust_files` keeps every `.rs` file except those under the project-root `vendor`. `src/vendor` and `src/book` are therefore still checked, and `book/`, `evidence/`, `target/` and `.git` are excluded upstream by discovery.
- **Parse failures.** `validate_rust_functions` pushes `cannot parse Rust source` onto both `errors` and `discovery_errors`. It does the same for an unreadable file, so a file is never skipped silently.
- **Which items can be covered.** `unreferenced_items` builds the outline with `RUST_PROFILE`. `item_kind` limits coverable items to `fn` (including trait methods and nested functions), `struct`, `enum` and `union`.
- **References that count.**
  - Only outline comments owned by the node count (`outline.comments` with `comment.owner`), plus closed fenced comment references (`comment_fences`).
  - String literals, enclosing modules and impl blocks do not count, because the comment-ownership rules do not attach them to the item.
  - `covering_reference` rejects `fixme` and `term` roles.
  - It accepts a `habeas:*` built-in only through `builtin.check(kind)`, so only {cite} of `habeas:util` counts.
  - It accepts a named example only when `example_references_requirement` holds.
  - It accepts requirements.
- **Coverage by evidence reads.** `EvidenceReads::load` and `add_record` collect the file, item and hash of the outline inputs from every evidence JSON file, including citation and site reviews. `covers` walks from the node up through its parents and requires the node's current `structural_hash`.
- **Error versus warning.** Only test functions without {test} (`untested_tests`) and Cargo examples become errors. Other uncovered items are returned as `UncoveredItem`s for warnings, and `in_tests` marks items in a `tests` module.

**Tests**
- **Item kinds, comment ownership, string and enclosing references, field and variant comments:** `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references`, `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately`, `structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside` and `locates_functions_after_unicode_text`.
- **Named examples must reference a requirement:** `an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement` and `a_test_reference_to_an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement`.
- **Current-hash rule:** `a_read_covers_an_item_only_with_its_current_hash`. In `tests/references.rs`, `items_named_by_recent_evidence_have_recent_coverage_whatever_their_hash` shows an enclosing `impl` node recorded in a review covering its method.
- **Parse failures, vendor and other excluded paths, and all `.rs` files:** `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures`, `discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference`, `disallowed_paths_are_skipped_and_projects_outside_git_scan_every_file` and `untracked_sources_are_not_validated_until_staged_and_status_lists_them`.
- **Built-in `habeas:util`:** `habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review` and `fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated`.
- **`{fixme}` does not cover:** `a_fixme_does_not_count_as_an_items_reference`.
- **Warning surface:** `status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form` and `replacing_a_record_that_stops_reading_an_item_warns_until_it_is_covered`.

**Notes**
- The stale-hash behaviour asserted in `items_named_by_recent_evidence_have_recent_coverage_whatever_their_hash` comes from the coverage history layer (`coverage.history`). The rule for this requirement, current hash only, is what `covers` implements.
- `missing_function_references` is `#[cfg(test)]` yet carries an {impl} reference. It is only a test wrapper over `unreferenced_items`, so I do not count it as a gap.

text: :::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} discovery
Habeas MUST find the references of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
in project source files, where {cite}`requirements.references.reference_contexts`
says they count, and MUST fail with the source file and line if a
name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped
roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST
consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in
the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in
both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git`
and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by
{cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and
generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
:::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
:::{req} text_search
The harness MUST expose a `ripgrep` tool with this interface:
```text
ripgrep({ pattern: String, path: String = ".", context: Integer = 2,
referencing: Optional<ReferenceScope> }) -> SearchResult
ReferenceScope {
selection: String,                     // full name or definition glob
roles: Array<Role> = ["impl", "test", "cite"],
scope: "node" | "file" = "file",
SearchResult { matches: Array<SearchMatch> }
SearchMatch {
file: String,
item: String,        // selector of the innermost outline node
kind: String,
lines: Array<{ text: String, matched: Boolean }>,
The tool MUST search the requested permitted file or directory using
ripgrep's regular-expression syntax and default case-sensitive search and ignore
rules. It MUST search in process using ripgrep's library crates, without
requiring an external `rg` executable, and MUST apply source-access policy while
walking files rather than filtering results afterwards. It MAY search files in
parallel; results MUST be ordered by path and then line regardless of
parallelism, so the same sources always produce the same inputs. Explicitly allowed paths and discovered generated-output directories MUST
be searched even when ignored or hidden; workspace disallow rules still apply.
`context`
MUST be nonnegative and specify how many lines before and after each matching
line to include, defaulting to two on each side. Windows MUST stop at file
boundaries, and overlapping windows in the same file MUST be merged. The result
MUST give one entry for each innermost outline node containing a match, where a
match in a comment belongs to the node the comment belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`: the node's file, selector
under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`, kind, and its matching
and context lines in source order, each marked as matching or not and redacted
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. Results MUST NOT give line
numbers; the model locates and cites code by selector. Separate windows within
one node MUST be distinguishable, such as by an elision line that is not
marked as matching. Search results MUST NOT become
evidence inputs and MUST NOT include definitions; the model-facing description
MUST tell the model to read with the `habeas` tool any node whose code its
conclusion relies on. Setting `context` to zero MUST return only matching lines.
With `referencing`, the tool MUST search only sources, within `path`, that carry
a reference in one of `roles` to a requirement or example the `selection`
matches under {cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`, including
anchors under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: with `scope` `node`, only
the outline nodes that contain or are named by those references, and with
`file`, their whole files. A selection matching no requirement or example, or an
unknown role or scope, MUST return an explanatory tool error. Its model-facing
description MUST explain `referencing`.
Search results MUST exclude files disallowed by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; explicitly requesting an excluded
path MUST be handled as a denial under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
No matches MUST return an empty array; invalid arguments or a failed search MUST
return an explanatory tool error.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
:::{req} coverage.tests
Every Rust function carrying a test attribute, `#[test]` or an attribute whose
path ends in `test` such as `#[tokio::test]`, including those in Cargo
integration-test targets, MUST carry a `{test}` reference to a requirement or
named example under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`, in a comment
attached to it or within its body. A test function without one MUST be a
validation error naming its file, line, and name.
:::{req} coverage.examples
Every Cargo example target, each `.rs` file directly under the package's
`examples/` directory, each `examples/<name>/main.rs`, and each `[[example]]`
`path` in `Cargo.toml`, MUST `{cite}` a named example of the book under
{cite}`requirements.examples.definition` in a comment in that file. An example
target without one MUST be a validation error naming the file.
:::{req} coverage.report
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
